title: Widget deprecation and attribution play slate
content:
Summary
Short working slate for how we retire, replace, and attribute dashboard widgets while keeping SLI continuity. Focus is on low-noise deprecation, operator handoff, and trace sampling adjustments for probes that detect user-visible regressions. Meant to be a lightweight playbook to run during a 2-week dashboard sprint.

Goals
- Avoid sudden blind spots when panels are removed.
- Maintain SLI continuity (no breaks in alerting or regression windows).
- Provide clear attribution for metrics so infra/rt/serving teams can act.
- Reduce query costs by consolidating and retiring redundant widgets.

When to deprecate a widget (quick checklist)
- Panel has < 5 manual opens/week (grafana opens) for 90 days OR
- Panels duplicate upstream tenant-level metrics already surfaced in a canonical dashboard OR
- Owner identifies high query cost without corresponding ops value.
- Product/CS confirms no downstream dependency (email or slack thread).

Pre-deprecation steps (1–2 week window)
- Owner adds a yellow banner in the panel and update panel description: "Marked for deprecation — feedback before YYYY-MM-DD".
- Announce in #observability and ping owners. Link: Confluence OBS-DRIVER-19.
- Add a feature-flag-like flag to dashboard metadata (dashboard annotation) indicating deprecation plan and date.
- Create a small synthetic probe (canary) that exercises the underlying query at a lower cadence (1/10th) so we keep data continuity if panel removed.
- Add metric-contract note to the metric doc (e.g., metric cols, cardinality hints).

Deprecation execution (day of removal)
- Replace panel with a single compact panel that points to canonical metric (owner, query snippet, and link to replacement). Keep it for 30 days as a redirect.
- Add alert mapping: ensure any alerts that referenced old panel/metric have a mapped replacement alert or a ticket created (Jira ENG-4321 style).
- Keep the synthetic probe for 30 days to ensure time series continuity and SLI checks continue working.

Post-deprecation (30–90 days)
- After 30 days, remove redirect panel and reduce probe cadence if not needed.
- If regressions observed tied to removed panel, reopen via rollback instructions (see below).
- Close the deprecation ticket and update metric ownership roster.

Attribution matrix (how to map who owns what)
- Host-level infra metrics (gpu-util, mem-used): infra.owners = infra-eng@redwood.com.
- Serving runtime (tokens/sec, kv-cache-hit-rate, batch-size-dist): serving-runtime team.
- API and routing (request-latency, 5xx-rate, region-fallback-rate): platform-api team.
- Quality signals (per-prompt hallucination-rate, rerank-loss): applied-ml/product-hosted-api (collab).
- Cost signals (token-cost-per-request, gpus-hours): finance + infra.
Note: maintain a single canonical metric doc per metric with owner and a fallback oncall alias.

Metric definition examples (suggested minimal contract)
- inference.request_latency_p50_ms: type=histogram / buckets; labels: model, deployment, region, route; owner: platform-api; intent: SLI for interactive P50.
- inference.kv_cache_hit_ratio: type=gauge; labels: model, tenant; owner: serving-runtime; intent: efficiency optimization for cost.
- inference.hallucination_flag_rate: type=counter (bool per-response); labels: model, eval_set; owner: applied-ml; intent: quality SLO.
Each metric definition must include: description, units, cardinality estimate, instrumentation pointer (file/line/GitHub PR).

Trace sampling play (balanced cost vs. fidelity)
Problems we see: full trace capture for every token request is prohibitively expensive and produces noisy spans. Need tiered sampling:
- High-fidelity sampling for SLI violations and anomalies (100% capture for requests that triggered an alert within 5m).
- Deterministic sampling for a small percentage (0.5%–1%) of traffic for baseline longitudinal analysis. Use hash(model, tenant, route) to ensure stable samples across time.
- Rate-limited ad-hoc sampling: operators can turn sampling to 100% for a specific tenant or deployment for live investigations via console toggle.
- Lightweight span-only traces: capture only high-level spans (no token-level span) for regular traffic to keep linkability but lower cardinality.

Heuristics and triggers
- If a request crosses token-cost threshold (e.g., > 5k tokens) OR latency > 95th percentile of model baseline -> increase sampling for that session.
- For multi-model fanout, capture the root request and per-model root spans but avoid token-level children unless flagged.
- For KV cache cold-starts, tag traces with kv_cold=true and sample at a higher rate.

Investigation runbook (operator-friendly)
1) Identify symptom: SLO alert or user complaint. Note time window + sample request ids.
2) Check synthetic probes & redirect panel. Is baseline probe failing?
3) Pull deterministic traces for the impacted window. Use query: "trace.service='inference' AND trace.tag.route='chat' AND duration>500ms"
4) If insufficient detail, flip ad-hoc sampling for tenant/route in console (create incident flag). Capture for 10 minutes.
5) Correlate with KV cache metrics, batch-size histograms, and model variant routing.
6) Open a triage ticket and assign to owner from attribution matrix.

Dashboard lifecycle cadence (recommendation)
- Quarterly dashboard audit: owners review panels, mark duplicates, and note cost-heavy queries.
- Weekly mini-sprint: rotate 2–3 low-traffic panels for consolidation.
- Monthly cost report: top 20 queries by data egress + compute time.

Notes to self / unresolved items
- Need a lightweight tagging scheme for dashboard panels so the console can list "deprecated_by" and "canonical_metric".
- How do we purge old synthetic probe data without breaking regression history? Maybe tiered retention.
- Should we add a "panel-cost" metric into Grafana for query-level cost attribution? (work with finance).

Action items (next 2 weeks)
- Create dashboard annotation schema RFC (Sofia). Link to GH PR telem/pull/212.
- Implement deterministic hash sampler prototype (Amir).
- Run a mini audit on "operator-quickcards" dashboard and propose 5 panel removals (Priya + Carlos).

Slack threads / references
- #observability: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/COBSERV123
- Confluence: OBS-DRIVER-19 (dashboard deprecation model)

If you want to test deprecation flow end-to-end, pick a non-critical dashboard and run through pre-deprecation steps this week. I'll draft the email template for owners.

-- end of slate --
